AR = antireflective 2.8.1 Technology Trends for Crystalline-Silicon PV Glass Solar glass requires a special formulation of low-iron sand to increase light transmission. These soda-lime-silica glasses contain silicon dioxide (65%–75%), sodium oxide (10%–20%), calcium oxide (5%–15%), and smaller quantities of aluminum oxide, magnesium oxide, antimony oxide, and cerium oxide (Thomsen et al. 2009; Chen et al. 2020). Iron oxide impurities must be kept below 0.1%, preferably less than 0.04% (Thomsen et al. 2009). Glass-glass modules are becoming the prevalent packaging scheme, capturing 40% market share in 2023, although glass-backsheet modules are still used in residential and commercial applications (Fischer et al. 2025). Glass thickness affects module durability. Front and back glass are typically 2.3 mm thick for glass-glass modules. For glass-backsheet configurations, the front glass is usually 3.2 mm thick (Fischer et al. 2024). In glass-glass modules, only the front-side glass has an antireflective coating. Because the diffuse light reaching the rear side is not as efficiently trapped by the antireflective coating, the coating is typically not worth the additional cost (Ovaitt et al. 2024). Traditionally, both front and back glass for c-Si modules are made through the rolled process (as opposed to the float process used for CdTe front glass) (Fischer et al. 2024; Palmiotti et al. 2025). Rolled glass is also called patterned glass owing to the patterning imparted by the rolls.
